title: Exact local work of Fourier estimation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. Every possible outcome of the confidence-parameter finite-family Fourier estimator has charged local work exactly $|\mathcal F|Mn+|\mathcal F|M+|\mathcal F|M(n+1)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used per coefficient at accuracy parameter $\varepsilon$ and total confidence parameter $\delta$.
hypotheses_covered: outcome belongs to the support of the estimator's output-and-cost distribution
